newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Port Arthur murderer not insane - court.
newsitem.headline: Australian Port Arthur murderer not insane - court.

text.p: Australian mass murderer Martin Bryant was not criminally insane when he gunned down 35 people at Port Arthur in April, but was suffering from a personality disorder, a court was told on Wednesday.
"There is no such (insanity) defence available to him," Prosecutor Damian Bugg told the Tasmanian Supreme Court, referring to the findings of a psychiatric report on Bryant.
Bryant two weeks ago week reversed his previous pleas and confessed to murdering 35 people at the Port Arthur historic convict site on the island state of Tasmania on April 28.
But Bryant's lawyer John Avery on Wednesday told the court his client would give no explanation for his killing spree.

"I am instructed to make no submissions or place before the court any explanation or reason for this massacre, other than can be gleaned from the medical material," Avery said at the end of a two-day sentencing hearing.
The court will sit again for sentencing on Friday.

A psychiatric report on Bryant before the court said the 29-year-old suffered from a personality disorder known as Asperger's Syndrome, which affects about three percent of the population, and in some ways is similar to autism.
Asperger's Syndrome cannot be treated and its origins are unknown.
The prosecution says Bryant planned the massacre for months and has asked for him to be jailed for life, without parole.

Bryant's lawyer Avery agreed that a life sentence would be right for the killer. "The accused revels in the notoriety he has achieved, but in a simple way he accepts the enormity of his actions," Avery said.
"Martin Bryant accepts that in all probability he will never be released from prison and will die there and he also accepts that will be not an inappropriate sentence," he said.
"An answer for the burning question 'why?' must for the timebeing remain with the accused," Avery added.

Since reversing his not-guilty pleas two weeks ago, Bryant has declined to give any reason for what the prosecution says was a well-laid plan to cause maximum carnage and slaughter at Port Arthur, a popular tourist spot on the site of an old jail.

In a police video interview played in court on Wednesday, Bryant showed the confused and erratic behaviour attributed to him in newspaper profiles of the killer. At one point he expressed sorrow for the injured, then joked about the massacre.
"You see, if people do not do these unfortunate things, you guys would not have a job," Bryant said.
At another point, he said: "I wish I had a few more friends. I did not have a great deal of friends at school." Later he told his interrogators: "I'll miss you".
Bryant taunted police during his first interview, telling them he was sure they would catch the killer.
"I'm sure you'll find the person who caused all this," Bryant said with a smile, and then mouthed the word "Me". But Bryant did not realise the police camera was still filming.

One of his police interviewers replied he did not find the comment funny. "You should have put that on recording," Bryant retorted. "Oh, it's still recording...," the detective said, seeming to surprise Bryant, who at one point in the interview appeared to be manacled to a metal chair.

On Tuesday, the court was told that Bryant took less than two minutes to slaughter 20 people, all at point-blank or close range as they ate their lunch at the Broad Arrow Cafe at Port Arthur. He later hunted victims in the nearby bush, executing a six-year-old girl as she hid behind a tree.
